name: Totagatic River
blurb: Totagatic River in Wisconsin between Wisconsin DNR-listed public accesses.

timing.note: A reviewed speed/flow calibration has not been established. Access and guide information remain available.

sections.putIn: Totagatic River Access — Town of Lenroot
sections.takeOut: Totagatic River Access — Town of Frog Creek
sections.notes: Paddle the Totogatic flowage from the Highway 27 access below Nelson Lake Dam to the Duck Pond Road landing upstream of Totogatic Dam. Both markers show approximate facility areas. Finish before the dam; do not follow the river through it. The 3.1-mile planning distance is preliminary, and shallow water and marsh vegetation can affect passage.

notices.title: Take out before Totogatic Dam
notices.text: Use the flowage-side landing at Duck Pond Road. The Area marker is upstream of the dam and does not pinpoint the water entry. Inspect the landing during your shuttle, keep clear of the spillway, and do not continue through the dam. This access map does not establish a portage.

sections.putIn: Totagatic River Access — Town of Frog Creek
sections.notes: Markers identify agency-listed access; the map states whether a landing or an approximate facility area has been reviewed. Mileage is preliminary, measured along USGS river geometry; it is not a surveyed paddling route. This is a long section and may require more than one day; plan daylight, supplies and legal overnight stops. Difficulty has not been independently rated for every section. Check current conditions, hazards and access with the managing agency before paddling.
sections.accessReview: Dam crossing/portage unresolved: Totogatic Wildlife, Colton and Minong Flowage. The Duck Pond Road area marker now identifies the upstream landing, not a downstream launch. No complete legal carry route across these barriers has been established; do not plan this as a continuous float.
sections.routeReview: This section includes Colton, Minong Flowage, Totagatic Wildlife and needs a closer check of the landing or portage. Consult the agency guide and signed access; do not assume you can paddle through a dam.
